messages:
devin: FYI I'm seeing a 10-25% p95/p99 regression on FlashPaged when KV cache hit rate is <60% after the kernel-chooser commit last night. Started at 09:12 UTC.
olivia: ugh. which commit? sha/branch?
devin: land: runtime/chooser@47c9a2 — introduced `prefer_fused_for_long_prefix` toggle.
sam: can you paste the quick perf numbers? rough is fine.
devin: baseline (before): p50=18ms p95=86ms p99=145ms\nafter: p50=19ms p95=104ms p99=189ms\n(bench: 8xA100, seq=2048, batch=4, kv_miss workload)
perf-bot: Ran perf/regression-suite on 8gpu-flash-2048. Link: https://perf.redwood/reports/17234 (summary attached)
maria: key observation from traces: lots of small-kernel fallbacks during prefix extension. kernel chooser flips between fused-flash -> paged-flash -> fallback-nonfused for certain seq-length + prefix sizes.
olivia: sounds like oscillation costs. any pattern with batching? maybe micro-batching causes chooser to see different seq distributions
devin: yes — when batch size >=3 we get a larger fraction routed to fused which is great for hits, but when a request has cold KV (many misses) runtime switches mid-request for tail tokens and we pay kernel swap overhead + cache miss penalties.
sam: can you share the sampling trace? a short snippet is fine
devin: pasted small snippet:\n```\n[ROOT] request id=abc123 seq=2048\n  tokens 0-512 -> fused_flash kernel (kv_cached=true)\n  tokens 513-1536 -> paged_flash kernel (kv_cached=false) -> prefetch triggered\n  tokens 1537-2048 -> fallback_kernel (nonfused) -> increased launch time\n```\nmaria: interesting — prefetch latency + kernel swap seems to drive tail p99. We saw a similar pattern in #prefetch-handoff tests a while ago.
infra-ops: quick question — is this across all GPUs? or only a subset with old cuBLAS drivers?
devin: repro on 3 different machine images (A100-v5, A100-v4); driver matched. Not driver-specific.
perf-bot: bisect candidates: 1) chooser heuristic change (47c9a2) 2) prefetch scheduling tweak (46b8f1) 3) kernel-launch backoff (45d7e0). Automated bisect in progress (step1: revert chooser toggle locally).
olivia: while bisect runs, can we reproduce locally with smaller hardware? use seq=1024 batch=2 maybe to speed iteration
devin: reproduced on local devbox (seq=1024 batch=2) with same relative delta. I'll drop a repro script: `tools/bench/run_flash_workload --seq 1024 --batch 2 --kv-pattern cold`.
sam: if revert chooser fixes it, we should consider a fallback policy: avoid switching kernels mid-request unless predicted benefit > threshold (ms saved > swap_cost). maybe add hysteresis.
maria: agree. add hysteresis + prefer keep-current unless >10% improvement predicted. also surface per-request kernel decision traces to console for easier debugging.
infra-ops: once bisect finishes, let's schedule a canary rollback on staging and run a 6h soak. Also add alert for sudden p95 jump on attention paths (current alert threshold is pretty high).
devin: created a short PR to add decision-hysteresis + debug logging: runtime/chooser#842 — running CI benchmarks now. If CI shows no regression we'll canary.
olivia: thanks. devin can you drop the raw nvprof flame snippet in the thread when available? would help quantify kernel-launch vs memory copy costs
devin: will do. for now tagging the thread with :mag: and adding to the perf board.
perf-bot: bisect update: reverted chooser locally -> p99 back to 146ms (~baseline). Next step: test hysteresis patch.
sam: nice. if hysteresis fixes it, rollout plan: staged flag off by default, enable on 5% of traffic, monitor p95/p99 for 12h, then expand.
maria: also add an E2E eval prompt set (long-prefix synthetic) to Redwood Optimize so this doesn't regress silently.
devin: noted. I'll follow up with a postmortem if rollback needed. thanks all :thumbsup:
